items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6p3: A high-speed train from Madrid to Seville crashed into a stationary train near Toledo, Spain, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens. The halted train had stopped due to a signalling computer failure, and a control-centre error let the moving train proceed into it. It's one of Europe's deadliest rail disasters in over a decade.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Protesters in Serbia stormed a television studio and confronted its editor-in-chief, after a student-led movement that had organized mass demonstrations won national elections. A regional public broadcaster separately apologized for years of one-sided, pro-government coverage, signaling a possible shift toward more independent media in the country.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: Egyptian authorities briefly detained and fined press-freedom figure Lina Attalah, editor of independent outlet Mada Masr, after a Cairo court convicted her of running an unlicensed website; she was released once Mada Masr paid a fine of about $53,500. The outlet's website was also ordered shut. Rights groups say the case signals an intensifying crackdown on Egypt's independent media.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm9q: Survivors described chaos after a Renfe high-speed train, ordered to proceed despite a signal failure, slammed into a halted Iryo train near Toledo, Spain, killing 68. Passengers were asleep, working or on their phones moments before the crash; some scrambled to break windows and escape the wreckage. The disaster has triggered anger over how the rail system handled the failure.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro, after fleeing to the US, posted on social media claiming to be Brazil's 'true president-elect' before deleting it. He had actually lost Sunday's election to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, making the claim baseless rhetoric amid his departure from the country.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/global-devel: Africa CDC director Jean Kaseya warned that an 'unprecedented' Ebola outbreak, now spanning three African regions with 10,000 cases and nearly 5,000 deaths, could spread internationally, including to the UK, unless more funding goes toward preparedness and treatment. He compared the risk to Covid-19's early spread from China, urging every country, not just African nations, to raise readiness levels now.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6kg: Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who flew to Miami after Sunday's election defeat, insisted he 'did not flee' Brazil but left for the country's sake, calling it political persecution. The US granted him visas after Brazil revoked his passport in a criminal probe, with Trump saying the US gave him 'a pass.' New president Lula criticized the secretive exit.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: Riot police were deployed in Madrid after the deadly train crash fuelled anger across Spain, with far-right demonstrators clashing with officers during an anti-government protest. Hundreds of protesters demanded the transport minister's resignation, questioning how authorities handled the disaster that killed 68 people.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/global-devel: The UK sanctioned 15 senior commanders from Sudan's warring Rapid Support Forces and Sudanese Armed Forces over suspected sexual violence during last year's siege of El Fasher. Up to 10,000 civilians were killed in two days as the RSF took the city. The move, marking the siege's anniversary, aims to hold both sides accountable.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmdx: Partial Israeli election results show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc leading with about 53 of 120 Knesset seats, short of a majority, against rival Gadi Eisenkot's bloc on 48. Arab-led parties, on course for an unprecedented 19 seats, could be kingmakers, though most Jewish parties rule out working with them.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/k: The Karnataka High Court criticized the state government for delays of up to 1,099 days in filing appeals, noting the irony that a 2023 law meant to cut red tape in government litigation has itself become bogged down by red tape. The remarks came while hearing four state appeals over a university staffing dispute.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/education/navodaya-: Admit cards for the Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Class 6 entrance exam (JNVST) 2027 have been released. The exam is scheduled for November 28, 2026, for admission to the 2027-28 academic session.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Quad defence ministers from India, the US, Japan and Australia reaffirmed their commitment to a free, open and secure Indo-Pacific on the sidelines of an ASEAN meeting in the Philippines. India's Rajnath Singh held separate talks with counterparts as the group tracks China's expanding military footprint. The talks follow a 10-year India-US defence framework, showing deepening security cooperation.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/internatio: A group of RSS supporters called 'RSS Friends' registered as a foreign agent of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh under the US Foreign Agents Registration Act, aiming to boost outreach in America. It listed RSS's Delhi headquarters as its 'foreign principal' but said it has no formal paid agreement with the organisation. Its activities will be informational and public-relations focused.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/uttarakh: Uttarakhand has declared a public holiday for female government employees on Karwa Chauth, following directions from Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami. The order applies to women employees across the state.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: India's Railway Board has reiterated orders to switch off power sockets in trains between 11pm and 5am, after a passenger's power bank exploded and caught fire aboard the Mumbai-Howrah Mail on October 24, halting the train for 15 minutes. The incident revealed lapses in staff compliance. All zonal railways must now strictly enforce the night-time shutdown.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/p: Poland is deepening ties with India as its 'strategic partnership' with China frays, following Polish PM Donald Tusk's visit to Delhi, the first by a Polish leader in 16 years. The two countries aim to raise bilateral trade from $6 billion to $10 billion. Poland's shift mirrors an EU trend of distancing from China over trade imbalances and Beijing's support for Russia.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/assam-ri: Assam Rifles chief Vikas Lakhera visited the India-Myanmar border and reviewed fencing work in Manipur. Manipur's chief minister had earlier raised concerns about border surveillance and inter-agency coordination at a NITI Aayog meeting in Delhi.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Delhi traffic police issued 4.53 lakh challans for invalid pollution-control certificates between January and October 27 this year, against 8.63 lakh for all of 2025, part of a five-fold rise since 2022. Officers say stricter enforcement aims to curb vehicle emissions ahead of the city's winter pollution season. The crackdown reflects Delhi's ongoing struggle to control air quality.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Nike launched its first running shoe designed specifically for India, the Vegam Run, which goes on sale on Flipkart from November 1. The move is part of Nike's push to tap India's running boom and open a new India campus, as it seeks growth to offset weakness in other key markets like China.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Nike unveiled the Vegam Run, its first shoe designed specifically for India, priced at about ₹3,795 and launching on Flipkart on November 1. Developed in roughly five months, it's part of CEO Elliott Hill's push to revive growth through locally designed products, as sales in China, about 15% of Nike's revenue, keep falling.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said she expects 'very few' of the roughly 60,000 employees offered a voluntary exit package to actually take it, citing strong growth opportunities within the company. The buyout is part of Microsoft's effort to reshape its workforce while continuing heavy investment in AI, rather than mass layoffs.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India's Union Cabinet approved a ₹10,000 crore Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to boost domestic container production through 2040. It also approved a rural development scheme through 2031 and a Khelo India scheme to support sports goods manufacturing through 2034. Together, the schemes reflect a push to build manufacturing capacity across logistics, rural development and sports.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-ma: Indian markets were set to open higher on Thursday as GIFT Nifty signaled a positive start, a day after the Sensex fell 352 points and Nifty slipped below 22,700. Stocks including Jio Platforms, Coal India, IndiGo, Trent and Meesho were in focus amid company-specific news and order updates. The mixed signals show investors weighing fresh corporate announcements against a choppy broader market.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmx2: Ahead of UK Chancellor John Healey's first Budget, the BBC spoke to people across income levels, from £4,062 to £150,000 a year, about their finances. One widow earning £30,000, raising a teenage son alone, said rising energy costs were squeezing her household despite subsidised rent, and she was frustrated no fuel duty cut was expected.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Tractor sales in India are projected to fall by up to 10% year-on-year as demand dries up on arid farms, even after an 8% rise to 610,000 units in the first half of the year. Dealers are also seeing sharp declines in entry-level cars and two-wheelers, which rely on large rural customer bases. The slowdown signals weakening rural demand.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: PNB Housing Finance reported a 6% rise in Q2 net profit to ₹617 crore, with net interest income up 15% to ₹878 crore and assets under management growing 17% to ₹98,210 crore. Gross non-performing assets, or bad loans, declined to 0.91% of its book. The results point to steady growth and improving asset quality in India's housing finance sector.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: Samsung posted a record quarterly operating profit of $80 billion (107.44 trillion won), up 783% year-on-year, as AI-driven demand for memory chips boosted earnings; its chip division alone contributed nearly all of that profit. Revenue rose 127% to 195.25 trillion won. Samsung warned the global memory chip shortage could deepen further in 2027, as AI infrastructure investment keeps outpacing industry supply.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: India extended its Production Linked Incentive scheme for textiles until 2033-34 and relaxed eligibility, cutting the minimum turnover requirement for manufacturers from ₹200 crore to ₹100 crore. A reopened application portal will accept new submissions from November 1 to December 31. The move aims to widen participation, especially among smaller manufacturers, to boost domestic textile investment.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/innodata-lays-off: US-based AI services firm Innodata laid off nearly 550 employees in India, about 5% of its global workforce, with additional cuts in the Philippines. A termination email cited a 'ramp-down' of a business assignment rather than performance issues, suggesting a major client pulled back a large project. The cuts add to uncertainty in the tech sector.
items.https://entrackr.com/news/bijnis-rebrand: B2B quick-commerce startup Bijnis rebranded as Zorit after raising about ₹27 crore ($2.84 million) led by Sparrow Capital, with existing investors Info Edge and WaterBridge also participating. Founded in 2015 as a marketplace connecting manufacturers with retailers, Zorit shifted to an inventory-led quick-commerce model in 2024, running 12 dark stores across 12 cities with deliveries in under an hour.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Meesho's quarterly losses narrowed as revenue grew in the second quarter of FY27, according to ET's newsletter roundup. Separately, Info Edge named Sanjeev Bikhchandani as its CEO.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/holiday-tribe-in-: Traveltech startup Holiday Tribe is in talks to raise about ₹50 crore ($5.2 million), with RPSG Capital Ventures among the prospective investors, though the round's size and participants could still change. The company, founded in 2022 by former MakeMyTrip executives, offers customised holiday planning and previously raised ₹25 crore in August 2025.
items.https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/astrotalk: Astrology platform Astrotalk's net profit jumped more than tenfold to ₹222 crore in FY26, as revenue grew 55% to cross ₹1,800 crore, with overseas revenue growing 2.6 times. Consultations, which connect users with astrologers via chat, call and video, made up 91% of operating revenue. Overseas growth now accounts for 34% of total revenue, up from 20% a year earlier.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Anthropic told California's governor that courts should have the power to block AI models deemed too risky. The company had itself faced US government restrictions, after the Trump administration ordered it to curb foreign access to its Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models over national security concerns, an order later lifted by the Commerce Department.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Steve Smith is expected to be fit to face New Zealand despite a joint injury that had troubled him since the second Test. He had been hampered in the lead-up and decided shortly before play at Newlands that he couldn't continue in that match, but scans have since cleared him for the next game.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: Brazilian forward Estevao is struggling for playing time at Chelsea under manager Xabi Alonso, a year after becoming a Premier League sensation with a last-minute winner against Liverpool. He didn't feature as Chelsea lost to Liverpool on penalties in the Carabao Cup, showing how quickly a breakout talent can fall down the pecking order.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/r: Tamil Nadu chased down a target of 128 to beat Railways by five wickets in their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D match, registering their second successive win. Vice-captain Andre anchored the chase after early jitters, while Railways spinners Toufik Mondal and Raj Choudhary fought hard with the ball.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: South Africa are dealing with fitness concerns as Kagiso Rabada battles stomach cramps and Marco Jansen nurses back stiffness. Jansen left the field after tea but returned soon after, while Rabada is expected to be back on day three.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: League Two side Fleetwood Town, the lowest-ranked team left in the Carabao Cup, will face either Everton or Newcastle in the quarter-finals after their upset win over Arsenal. Holders Manchester City will host League One's Bradford City, while Liverpool face Bournemouth and Crystal Palace play Sunderland in the other ties.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/t: India's T20 side has four equally aggressive opening options — Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Ishan Kishan — giving it unusual batting depth at the top. Abhishek Sharma has been especially destructive, almost guaranteed to hit a six if he faces at least 10 balls, as shown again at Wellington while India trailed 0-2 in a five-match series.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/28/micros: Microsoft disclosed for the first time that Azure's cloud revenue reached $33.2 billion in the July-September quarter, up 48% year-on-year, beating analyst estimates. Azure, where businesses rent computing power to run applications and AI models, now makes up roughly 36% of Microsoft's $92.3 billion quarterly revenue. The disclosure lets investors compare Azure directly against AWS and Google Cloud.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Instagram head Adam Mosseri said public negativity toward AI is 'going to get worse,' not just among young people and creatives but more broadly. Speaking on a podcast about Instagram's new video features, he linked the backlash to a widespread 'fear of being left behind' as AI reshapes work and creative industries.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/10/googl: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, an upgraded version of its Gemini 4 Argon model released just two weeks earlier, though it isn't yet available to the public. Google says Carbon makes major gains in cybersecurity, including better vulnerability detection and code that is twice as likely to be bug-free as Argon's.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: A survey by MIT Technology Review Insights found that while every organization uses AI to some degree, fewer than one in five (16%) are getting transformative value from it, with 23% seeing minimal or no returns. Most are still piloting AI or using it for simple tasks like co-pilots. The gap suggests deployments fail from a lack of business context.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/28/google: Google is expanding ads within its AI-powered Search features to international markets, aiming to turn AI into a new revenue stream as core search ad growth slows. The move came alongside Alphabet's third-quarter results, showing revenue up 25% to $127.6 billion, even as search ad growth decelerated to 12% from 19% earlier in the year; shares fell 8% on the news.
items.https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/1021405: Akai is embracing fan-made 'vibe-coded' mods for its unreleased MPC Sample Key by giving modders early access to the device's open-source firmware. The budget 37-key sampler will let users run custom synths and firmware tweaks, building on community hacks already seen on its MPC Sample. The move shows a hardware maker leaning into open customization culture rather than locking down its product.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/10/googl: Google's AI Mode gave evasive, non-committal answers when asked directly who won the 2020 and 2024 US presidential elections, instead pointing users to official sources like the Federal Election Commission rather than naming the actual winners. The same caution did not apply to an older query about the 2012 election, raising questions about whether AI tools dodge politically sensitive facts.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: Living digital twins, virtual replicas of physical operations, are helping industrial plants move beyond passive monitoring toward real-time intervention in their own operations. Unlike earlier digital twins that only simulated or observed, these systems combine high-fidelity modeling with the ability to act through real control systems. The shift signals more autonomous industrial AI, raising questions about how much control to hand over.

This opinion piece argues that AI and tech policy focuses too much on dramatic worst-case harms, like chatbots encouraging suicide, while ignoring everyday damage such as unhealthy attachment to AI companions or feeds designed to maximize scrolling. It warns that clearing such low bars lets companies avoid addressing subtler, cumulative harms to how people think and interact.
items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1020769/me: Meta signaled it may again delay new business terms, already pushed from October 30th to November 20th, after publisher backlash over fears the terms would let it train AI on content from Facebook and Instagram. Meta says it won't change policy without consulting industry groups, though it removed explicit 'training' language. Experts say that may not rule out AI training on publisher content.
items.https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/10/anthr: Anthropic's newly filed IPO prospectus includes a 93-page, 70,000-word 'Risk Factors' section detailing hundreds of potential threats, including scenarios where its AI could blackmail people or even threaten humanity. Alongside standard risks like competition and costs, the filing flags risks specific to Anthropic and the broader AI boom. The candid list shows AI firms going public must disclose extreme, even existential, risks.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: As Anthropic files its 335-page IPO prospectus, about 100 pages of which cover risks, this piece argues the company has built an effective public narrative about AI's transformative and dangerous potential. It cites cofounder Jack Clark's claim at an IMF meeting that the 'singularity,' where technology outpaces human control, has arrived. Anthropic's storytelling, it argues, shapes perception as much as its technology.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/28/anthro: Anthropic launched new reporting tools letting enterprise customers see what their AI spending is buying, using internal analytics and employee surveys to show what teams produced, what it cost, and where workflows broke down. The move follows financials showing Anthropic turned an operating profit last quarter and saw customer spending grow ninefold year-on-year, ahead of its planned IPO.
items.https://inc42.com/resources/why-indian-a: Indian AI startups raised over $1.1 billion in the first nine months of 2026, even as founders increasingly look to the US for enterprise customers, capital and global expansion. Reo.Dev, for instance, raised $11.3 million partly to expand US sales while keeping most of its team in India. Founders now face a trade-off between global reach and keeping development rooted at home.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/cognizant-in-talk: Cognizant is reportedly in talks to invest in Indian AI startup Sarvam AI as part of a $300 million fundraise that could value it at $3.5-4 billion, more than double its previous $1.5 billion valuation. It would make Cognizant the second IT services firm on Sarvam's cap table after HCLTech, which invested $150 million in June, as IT firms buy AI stakes.
items.https://inc42.com/features/finding-india: This piece argues India's AI opportunity lies less in building compute-heavy foundation models and more in supporting infrastructure like power delivery, cooling systems and faster data connections for data centres. It notes Indian deeptech investing has long been held back by a lack of patient capital. India could carve a differentiated role in AI infrastructure with more patient capital.
